chief_complaint: frothy yellow-green discharge with strawberry cervix
hpi_details: A 74-year-old woman presents with recent frothy yellow-green vaginal discharge and a strawberry cervix on examination.
ideas: She thinks the discharge and irritation might just be a stubborn yeast infection or a reaction to wearing daily panty liners.
concerns: She is worried that the abnormal green discharge could be a sign of cervical or uterine cancer at her age.
expectations: She hopes to receive a prescription cream or pill to clear up the bad odor and discharge before her family visits for the weekend.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Trichomoniasis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days, with concurrent treatment of sex partners, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Trichomoniasis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bacterial vaginosis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Sexually transmitted infection requiring partner treatment.
management_principles: Oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days; treat sex partners concurrently
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

must_ask.say: Can you describe the discharge: its color, consistency, and any odor?
Do you have any itching, burning, or pain with urination?
Do you have a new or multiple sexual partners recently?
Has your partner had any symptoms like discharge or irritation?
We'll treat you with metronidazole 500 mg twice daily for 7 days. Your partner also needs treatment, and avoid sex until treatment is complete.

history.answer: I've noticed a strange, yellowish-green discharge with small bubbles coming from my vagina for the past few days, and it feels quite irritated down there.
It began about four or five days ago and has gradually become heavier and more irritating.
No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life, and I haven't used any medications or creams to treat it yet.
The discharge is yellowish-green and distinctly frothy, with tiny bubbles, rather than thick or cheesy.
It has a noticeable, foul odor that smells quite bad, though I wouldn't necessarily say it smells like dead fish.
Yes, I have intense itching and a burning sensation around the outside of my private area that bothers me throughout the day.
It looks slightly red and swollen around the outside, and it feels tender when I wipe.
I went through menopause over twenty years ago, so I haven't had a period in a very long time.
I feel some burning and stinging when I urinate, especially when the urine washes over the raw skin outside.
No, I have not had any bleeding, spotting, or brownish discharge at all.
No, I do not have any lower belly cramps or pelvic pain, and I have not had any fever or chills.
Yes, intercourse was distinctly painful and uncomfortable when we tried a few days ago, so we had to stop.
I am sexually active with a new male partner I started seeing about two months ago, and we have not been using condoms.
He recently mentioned having some mild burning when he passes urine, but he didn't think much of it and hasn't seen a doctor.
No, I have not taken any antibiotics or steroid medications recently, and I do not have diabetes.
No, I never douche, and I only wash the outside area with plain warm water in the shower.
I wear loose cotton undergarments, avoid tight clothing, and haven't used tampons since my periods stopped decades ago.
Since I have been menopausal for many years, we do not use any birth control pills, intra-uterine devices, or other contraception.
I had regular Pap smears throughout my life and they were always normal, though my last one was several years ago, and I never had the HPV vaccine.
I went through menopause around age 50; I have had occasional mild vaginal dryness over the years, but this current heavy discharge and burning are completely different.
I thought maybe it was just a bad yeast infection or irritation from the panty liners I've been wearing every day.
At my age, seeing this awful colored discharge makes me terrified that it could be cancer down there.
I just hope you can prescribe some medicine to get rid of this odor and discharge before my grandkids come over this weekend.
I have generally been very healthy and have no history of high blood pressure, diabetes, heart disease, or liver problems.
I have never had any surgeries, and I have never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, or health supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials like latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only drink an occasional glass of wine during social gatherings, perhaps once or twice a month.
I am retired and live at home in a quiet neighborhood.
There is no family history of cervical, uterine, or ovarian cancer, or any other significant illnesses in my family.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 124/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.7°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Flat, non-distended abdomen with no scars, rashes, or visible peristalsis.
Soft, non-tender to light and deep palpation throughout the abdomen including the suprapubic area; no palpable masses or muscular guarding.
No rebound tenderness elicited in any quadrant.
No costovertebral angle tenderness elicited on gentle percussion bilaterally.
Erythema and mild edema of the vulva and introitus; superficial excoriations present without chancres, blisters, or ulcers.

Speculum exam reveals copious frothy, greenish-yellow discharge and punctate mucosal hemorrhages across the cervix (strawberry cervix); bimanual exam reveals no cervical motion tenderness and no adnexal tenderness or fullness.
